rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and identify limiting peak pairs while targeting a short run. A midpoint temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.
Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the crowded central peaks gain resolution from a shallower slope. The last peak should remain near or below 10 minutes, avoiding a time penalty.

The limiting pair improved strongly with a shallower gradient, so reduce the slope further while raising the starting organic fraction to remove low-organic transit time. This should bring the remaining pair toward baseline resolution while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes.
Injection 3 achieved the maximum possible CRF. Raise temperature by 5 C to test whether the fully resolved separation can be shortened while preserving R ≥ 1.5 for the limiting pair.

The limiting pair converged sharply at 45 C; testing 60 C may separate it again after an elution-order reversal and shorten the run. Injection 3 remains the maximum-score fallback while we check for new critical pairs.

Test 55 C as a selectivity compromise: the central pair may have separated after crossing, while the pair crowded at 60 C may regain sufficient spacing. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate temperature effects and seek a shorter maximum-score separation.

Slightly flatten the gradient at 55 C to improve the nearly resolved pair at R = 1.41. The current 8.54-minute last peak leaves room for this adjustment while targeting full resolution before 10 minutes.

Use a gradient slope between injections 6 and 7 by lowering the endpoint to 0.90. This should retain baseline resolution for both limiting pairs while bringing the last peak out sooner than injection 7.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 8’s slope to test a shorter separation at the maximum CRF. Monitor the early peaks for excessive compression and the two limiting central pairs for selectivity changes.

Lowering the starting organic fraction should improve early retention and may restore spacing in the pair that compressed when phi0 increased. Combine this with a steeper gradient to seek a faster fully resolved separation than injection 8.

Shorten only the gradient to test whether injection 10’s full resolution survives further compression. Both limiting pairs are above threshold, and this run will establish whether a faster maximum-score method is available at the same temperature.

Reduce the endpoint to give a slope between injections 10 and 11, targeting recovery of the R = 1.29 pair while retaining the shorter separation. The endpoint remains comfortably above the estimated organic fraction at which the last peak elutes.

Increase the slope slightly from injection 12 to shorten elution while aiming to preserve both limiting pairs above R = 1.5. The 0.75 endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution composition, so all compounds should still elute during the gradient.

With maximum CRF already secured, explore a cooler, steeper-gradient regime for a potentially faster fully resolved separation. Cooling may separate the temperature-sensitive central peaks, but this run will also check for new limiting pairs as elution order changes.

Return to the favorable 55 C regime and test whether a lower starting organic fraction can preserve central-pair selectivity with a faster gradient. This explores a shorter separation while retaining injection 13 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Lengthen injection 15’s gradient to improve the limiting R = 1.00 pair while checking that the other central pair remains above 1.5. This may yield full resolution sooner than the current fastest maximum-score method at 7.76 minutes.

Test a steeper gradient at 60 C to see whether the pair nearly coeluting in injection 5 separates on the opposite side of an elution-order reversal. This explores a substantially faster regime while retaining injection 16 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten the gradient to test whether the remaining close pair continues to separate in this fast, high-temperature regime. Monitor the neighboring R = 1.62 pair closely, since further compression may make it limiting.

Test an intermediate cooler temperature with a moderate gradient to seek a faster fully resolved selectivity window between the crowded 30 C result and the successful 40 C method. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this run explores an alternative rather than replacing the validated methods.

Preserve injection 16’s successful slope while trimming the unused high-organic end of the gradient. The last peak’s estimated elution composition is 0.57, so this should retain maximum CRF and the approximately 7.60-minute separation with a shorter programmed gradient.

Explore the remaining low-temperature selectivity regime to see whether the crowded central peaks separate after further elution-order changes. Maximum CRF is already secured; this tests an alternative that may still elute fully within 10 minutes.

Preserve injection 3’s successful gradient slope while shifting the organic window upward to shorten retention. At 40 C, the early peaks may retain sufficient separation; this run will test whether the central limiting pair also remains fully resolved.

Test the unexplored 50 C selectivity at the fast gradient used in injection 17. This checks whether cooling improves the limiting pair without creating another overlap, while retaining the confirmed maximum-score methods as fallbacks.

Flatten injection 22’s gradient to improve its sole limiting pair at R = 1.20. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially providing another maximum-score method with better retention of the early peaks than the high-temperature alternatives.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower version of injection 12, aiming to increase the slope-sensitive pair’s resolution while keeping the other limiting pair above 1.5 and the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 20 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.
